wi_adidas_wall.blurb: Adidas Wall is a sport crag on Grandad Bluff above La Crosse, Wisconsin, with 13 bolted lines that run from 5.8 up to 5.10, most of them at 5.9 and 5.10. That makes it a friendly place for newer leaders and those working through the low double digits. The face is clean and faces west, so it catches sun for most of the afternoon, and a flat rock shelf at its foot gives you somewhere to flake a rope and sit between burns. A long, easy boulder traverse also runs along the base, handy for warming up. It is one of several walls reached by the bluff's bike trails.

wi_05_lost_face_area.blurb: Lost Face Area sits on the West Bluff of Devil's Lake in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range, just north of Prospect Point along the Prospect Point Rampart, a cliff known for some of the longest climbs at the lake. Thirteen routes here are mostly traditional leads, with a few top-rope lines. The bulk of them fall between 5.6 and 5.8, so it suits climbers building up on gear, while a handful of harder lines reach into the 5.10s and beyond for those who want a stiffer test. Expect a tall face with overhanging sections and a crowd on the nearby point.

wi_whaler_s_rock.blurb: Whaler's Rock is a bouldering spot on the East Bluff at Devil's Lake, within the Lost & Found section of the bluff's southern half. A big block with several lines on it anchors the area, backed by a short cliff band above the Mirror Talus Field and a few extra boulders. Thirteen problems range from VB-level warm-ups to a single hard V7, and the middle of the spread sits around V4, so there is something for most strength levels. It is among the first rocks you meet when arriving from below, and it lies underneath the Old Man and the Awning boulders.

wi_triple_tower_wall.blurb: Triple Tower Wall is a short wall deep in the woods of Steinke Basin at Devil's Lake, in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range, with three small towers at its east end. Most of the 13 climbs are boulder problems, ranging from V0 up to a single V8, with the bulk in the V0 to V4 range. A couple of top-rope lines and one trad route round it out. The easiest way to find it is to locate Steinke Wall first and work from there, since the basin's trails are faint and a GPS helps. Several problems here are tall enough to feel like highballs.

wi_surprise_boulder.blurb: Surprise Boulder is a single block on the South Bluff at Devil's Lake in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range, perched on the spine of a small tree-covered ridge above Messenger Creek. It carries 13 problems. Most are gentle, from VB through V3, and one standout is a V8 for the strong. Because the boulder is hidden by trees it comes as a surprise, but the walk from the parking lot is short. Finding it first makes it easy to locate the other boulders on the ridge, including Lil' Surprise and the lower Meth Mouth problems.

wi_river_edge.blurb: River Edge is a small bouldering area tucked beside the river in Lime Kiln Park, Grafton, Wisconsin. Reaching it takes a steep scramble down from the path, and getting back up with crash pads is harder than going in, so leave daylight for the exit. The 13 problems run from easy VB-type moves to V6, though most land between V1 and V4, which suits climbers looking for moderate circuits. It is secluded and quiet apart from the river noise, but in summer it can get overgrown and buggy.
